label: winner or champion of
definition: Argument 1 won competition/award 2 or holds its championship.
scope_notes: The win/champion family dominates identifiable semantics; movement and presence are substantial competing themes. Mere participation, reaching an event or winning one stage does not imply winning the whole event. Political office is outside this preserved award/competition scope.

facts.reason: Ullrich explicitly wins the Tour and is called its champion and winner. A stage-win row alone would not suffice, but direct whole-event paths do.
Kisselgoff reviews a season premiere associated with Dance Theater; no award or competition win is expressed.
Mets have a World Series victory and explicitly win the World Series title.
Yankees explicitly win the World Series; the participation path is additional evidence, not the basis of support.
Reagan leaves or brings something to Washington; neither row concerns a competition/award win.
